item.description:
S&P puts Nvidia’s AA rating on downgrade watch

S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia’s AA issuer and senior unsecured debt ratings on CreditWatch Negative. It cited concerns about board independence, oversight and reliance on CEO Jensen Huang. S&P said it could cut the ratings within 90 days if governance concerns persist.

item.description:

item.title: U.S. Bitcoin reserve bill reaches House calendar H.R. 8957 was reported with ame
item.description:
U.S. Bitcoin reserve bill reaches House calendar

H.R. 8957 was reported with amendments on November 24. If enacted, it would give Treasury 180 days to set up a Bitcoin reserve and a separate digital asset stockpile. The bill would require a 20-year minimum hold for reserve BTC.

item.title: Nvidia agrees to $290M in proposed mining-related settlement Bloomberg Law repor
item.description:
Nvidia agrees to $290M in proposed mining-related settlement

Bloomberg Law reports that Nvidia agreed to pay $290M to resolve a securities class action. Investors alleged the company understated how much crypto mining drove demand for its gaming GPUs. The lead plaintiffs asked a federal court in California to grant preliminary approval. The deal still requires court approval.

https://news.bloomberglaw.com/securities-law/nvidia-settles-investor-suit-over-crypto-mining-for-290-million

item.description:

item.description:
SBI Solana Global begins operations in Japan

SBI Holdings, SMBC Group and the Solana Foundation completed agreements for a joint venture. Formerly SBI R3 Japan, SBI Solana Global has begun operations. It will focus on stablecoin payments, tokenizing financial and real-world assets, and on-chain asset management. It starts in Japan and plans to expand across Asia.

item.description:

item.description:
CFTC adopts reporting rules for certain event contracts

The final rule covers certain fully collateralized contracts. Market and trade data requirements start 60 days after Federal Register publication. Large-trader reporting starts no earlier than July 26, 2027. Exchanges have 12 months from publication to collect trader details, including occupation and employer.

https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9330-26

item.title: CFTC staff outlines how crypto can count toward operating reserves Staff says de
item.description:
CFTC staff outlines how crypto can count toward operating reserves

Staff says derivatives venues and clearinghouses can count BTC, ETH and payment stablecoins toward resources for 12 months of operating costs. Haircut benchmarks are at least 20% for BTC and ETH and 2% for payment stablecoins.

The advisory leaves the separate cash and liquid securities requirement in place.

https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9331-26
